accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE 2013 national curriculum, English Appendix 2 (Year 4: 'Standard English forms for verb inflections instead of local spoken forms [for example, we were instead of we was, or I did instead of I done]') and the spoken language statement on using Standard English. was/were agreement (you were for singular you), the simple past vs past participle split (did/done, saw/seen, came/come, went/gone, wrote/written) and the ain't mapping (isn't/aren't for be, hasn't/haven't for have, with got signalling have) were checked in the Cambridge Grammar of English and Crystal's Rediscover Grammar. The lesson frames local forms as consistent dialect grammar, following Trudgill's description of non-standard English dialects, not as errors.

misconceptions.evidence: The predictions and feedback target the documented slips: you was for one person (step 1 prediction 'You ___ brilliant', feedback 'It is always you were, even for one person'), I done/we done with no helper (step 2 prediction 'We ___ it yesterday'), overcorrection to has did / has came (challenge tag 'over', step 2 feedback 'I have did is not Standard English'), I seen and he come (step 3 and the recount), and the wrong replacement for ain't (step 4 and challenge 'aint': got shows it means haven't).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagstdv is built on this topic's own mechanism: a was/were post, a did/done gap whose helper word (has, have, had) is shown or missing, a stand-alone vs after-a-helper sort of past forms, an ain't swap with four contractions, tapping local forms in a spoken recount that change in place, and a setting sort for when Standard English is expected. flagsva (415) sorts verb + s by subject, flagirrpast (770) builds irregular past forms from the present, flagtense (411) moves between tenses and flagdial (Dialects & Registers) sorts registers; none uses the helper-word rule. lab_distinct passed under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rule comes from the helper chip: the same sentence appears twice, 'I ___ my homework' with no helper and 'I have ___ my homework' with a lit have chip, and the wrong choice returns 'With no has, have or had, use did' or 'After have, use done'. Sorting saw/seen, went/gone and came/come into the two trays then shows the same pattern for other verbs, and the recount turns we was → were, done → did, seen → saw and come → came in place so the finished paragraph is readable as Standard English.

predictions.evidence: Two predictions each hold a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'You was brilliant' for one friend (step 1 sorts 'you (one friend)' into were) and 'We done it yesterday' (step 2 shows done only after a helper word). The completion line names the learner's own pick.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions; every wrong option has its own message: 'was' (we means more than one), 'be' (this happened in the past), 'over' (after has, have or had use done, seen, come), 'helper' (this form needs has, have or had), 'you' (you always takes were), 'aint' (got shows ain't means have) and 'agree' (they takes have, not has).

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences with a matching example for each rule ('did stands on its own: I did my homework.'); measured kid grade 1.6 against the family limit of 5.0 and adult 5.8 against 10.0 after splitting long sentences. The term past participle appears only in the adult text; the child-facing rule is 'needs a helper word'. The recount header was shortened to 'Tap the 4 local verbs (n found)' after the 360 px screenshot showed it shrinking.

no_filler.evidence: Every kid sentence states a rule or gives an example; the adult text gives the Year 4 requirement with its own examples, the stand-alone vs participle rule, a note on respecting home dialect, the named mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate found no filler phrases and the explanation is under 12% the same as any other lesson, including Subject-verb agreement (415) and Irregular past tense verbs (770).

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark for all seven steps before and after Show me: the subject card is 54 px tall over two side-by-side trays, the did/done gap puts the rest of the sentence on its own line on narrow screens, the four ain't tiles fit one row, the 21-word recount wraps into six rows of 40 px tiles, and the setting card fits the width. The walkthrough passed on iPhone 13.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button below (was / were, did / done with the full sentence in its aria-label, both trays, the four contractions, one button per recount word not yet fixed, both settings), and tapping a tray also posts the card. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) found no violations in either theme on desktop and iPhone 13.

Crystal, D. (2004) Rediscover Grammar: Standard English and regional forms
